clue.text: The writer twice revealing an element of culture

indicators.note: twice tells us to write the setter's self-reference two times over

parts.note: the writer of the clue refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: An author keeps referring to themself, which somehow reveals something about culture.
explanation.definitionFit: A meme is a unit of cultural information, an idea or behaviour passed from person to person.

clue.text: Participating in that act, I construct plan

indicators.note: participating in means the letters are taking part inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Someone involved in a stage act devises a scheme for it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a scheme or method devised to achieve a particular end.

clue.text: Legal document that can be read two ways

definitions.note: a signed and sealed legal instrument; the setter uses the definition itself as the palindrome

indicators.text: that can be read two ways
indicators.note: read two ways means the word reads identically forwards and backwards

parts.note: a signed and sealed legal instrument; the setter uses the definition itself as the palindrome

explanation.surface: A legal paper with an ambiguous meaning, open to two interpretations.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests ambiguous legal wording; really the word is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed is a signed legal instrument, such as one transferring property.

clue.text: Lover is worn out with minimal energy

parts.note: worn out means old, past its best

indicators.note: minimal takes only the smallest part of energy, its opening letter

explanation.surface: A lover is exhausted and has hardly any energy left.
explanation.walkthrough: ISOLDE is the lover of Tristan in the medieval legend and Wagner's opera.
explanation.definitionFit: Isolde is the famous lover in the tragic romance of Tristan and Isolde.

clue.text: Refined style associated with good girl

parts.note: the cut of a garment is its style
lass is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: A polished manner of speaking attributed to a well-behaved young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refined style' looks like one phrase, but 'style' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut-glass accent is a precise, upper-class way of speaking, hence posh or polished.

clue.text: What could make Carol happy is questionable

indicators.note: could make says these letters can be rearranged to form something else

explanation.surface: Whatever might cheer up Carol is a matter of doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: An apocryphal story is of doubtful authenticity, widely told but probably untrue.

clue.text: Worm, harmless coiling round, getting into knot

indicators.note: getting into puts the turned word inside the word for knot

parts.note: a node is a knot or knob, as on a stem

indicators.note: coiling round turns the word for harmless back on itself

parts.note: a tame animal is harmless

explanation.surface: A worm, though harmless, twists itself into a knot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coiling round' suggests the worm's own wriggling, but it signals that the word for harmless runs backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Nematodes are roundworms, a large phylum of slender unsegmented worms.

clue.text: Tricky cut into poor ground that's rocky

indicators.note: tricky suggests the letters are awkwardly mixed up

explanation.surface: A difficult cut made into poor, stony land.
explanation.definitionFit: An outcrop is rock that emerges above the surface of the surrounding land.

clue.text: Defeats — six on the cricket field?

definitions.meaning: to stump someone is to baffle or beat them
a cricket match has two wickets of three upright posts each, six posts in all

explanation.surface: Losses, perhaps six of them, suffered on the cricket field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'six' suggests a hit for six runs; really it counts the wooden posts at both ends of the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Stumps are the three upright posts of each wicket; to stump also means to baffle or defeat.

clue.text: Do better than that? Go away!

definitions.meaning: to beat something is to surpass it, and 'it' stands for that
an order to leave, a curt dismissal

explanation.definitionFit: Beat it is slang for leave at once, and literally means surpass that thing.

clue.text: Mission of editor reversing what predecessor left in place?

indicators.note: reversing turns the editor abbreviation back to front

parts.note: a legacy is what someone leaves behind for those who follow

explanation.surface: An editor's task is to undo whatever the previous editor left behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A delegacy is a body of delegates sent with authority, much as a mission or deputation is.

clue.text: Medical treatment that is shocking!

parts.note: shocking here means delivering electric shocks, not outrageous

explanation.surface: An outraged exclamation about scandalous medical care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shocking' seems to mean outrageous; literally the therapy uses electric current.
explanation.definitionFit: This therapy treats patients with electric currents, so it really does deliver shocks.

clue.text: Mediocre and negligent leader getting dumped — fantastic result

indicators.note: the leader getting dumped means the word for negligent loses its first letter

parts.note: slack means careless or negligent

indicators.note: fantastic suggests the letters of result are wildly rearranged

explanation.surface: A dull, careless leader is sacked, and the outcome is splendid.
explanation.walkthrough: SLACK loses its first letter to give LACK, and 'fantastic' turns RESULT into LUSTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacklustre describes something dull, uninspired and lacking brilliance or vitality.

clue.text: Object of phobia?

definitions.meaning: an object is an item, an article
having a strong fear or obsession about something is informally having one of these about it

explanation.definitionFit: A thing is any object, and to have a thing about spiders is to have a fixation or phobia.

clue.text: Acoustic effect needed by the choirmaster

indicators.note: needed by says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A choir director wants reverberation in the hall.
explanation.definitionFit: Reflected sound heard again after a delay is the classic acoustic phenomenon.

clue.text: Following behind speaker, I love to offer something musical

indicators.note: following behind places the next letters after the word for speaker

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
O is love, a nil score in tennis

explanation.surface: Someone trailing a public speaker declares their wish to provide some music.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large-scale musical work for choir, soloists and orchestra, usually on a sacred theme.

clue.text: Impression created by fast runs, nothing extreme

indicators.note: nothing extreme removes the letters at both ends of the word for fast runs

parts.note: sprints are short fast runs

explanation.surface: A mark left by someone running quickly, nothing too excessive.
explanation.definitionFit: A print is a mark or copy made by pressing, just as an impression is.

clue.text: The inadequate oarsman or shot-putter?

indicators.note: inadequate means falling short, so the word The loses its last letter

parts.note: a rower pulls an oar

explanation.surface: Is this a feeble rower, or an athlete who throws the shot?
explanation.definitionFit: A shot-putter is an athlete who hurls the heavy shot, so is a thrower in athletics.

clue.text: Note old part of London

parts.note: soh is the fifth note of the tonic sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Take note of an old district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: SOHO is a district in London's West End, known for nightlife and theatres.
explanation.definitionFit: Soho is a lively district in the West End of central London.

clue.text: Dealing awkwardly with what may be the paper's opinion piece

indicators.note: awkwardly suggests the letters of Dealing are clumsily rearranged

parts.note: the word 'the' that follows is an example of a grammatical article, so this phrase points to that word

explanation.surface: Handling the newspaper's editorial clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' does double duty: it is part of the definition and also the definite article that 'what may be' points to.
explanation.definitionFit: A leading article is a newspaper's editorial, setting out the paper's own view.

clue.text: More than one plant is seen covering hillside?

indicators.note: covering means the word is wraps around the hillside word

parts.note: a rise is a slope or upward incline of ground

explanation.surface: Several plants are spotted carpeting a slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Irises are flowering plants with sword-shaped leaves, here in the plural.

clue.text: A biro's possibly used to make line on map

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A ballpoint pen might be used to draw a line on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobar is a line on a weather map joining places of equal atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Shock when century is obtained by Leicestershire's No. 11

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as he arrived'
a ton is a hundred, in cricket a century of runs

indicators.note: No. 11 takes the eleventh letter of Leicestershire

explanation.surface: Amazement when a hundred runs are scored by Leicestershire's last batsman.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the No. 11 is the final, usually weakest batsman, so a century from him would astonish; here it is the eleventh letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish someone is to amaze or stun them, which is to shock them.

clue.text: Cry of bird descending from end of branch

indicators.note: in a down answer, descending from puts the bird below the letter from branch
end of takes the final letter of branch

parts.note: an owl is a bird

explanation.surface: A bird's call as it drops down from the tip of a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A howl is a long loud wail or cry, of pain, grief or laughter.

clue.text: Awkward Norse character concealing love

indicators.note: concealing means the god's name hides the next piece inside it

parts.note: Woden is the Anglo-Saxon name for Odin, the chief Norse god
O is love, a nil score in tennis

explanation.surface: A clumsy Scandinavian figure hiding his affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden describes stiff, stilted behaviour, as in an awkward acting performance.

clue.text: Times to strike out, launching enterprise finally

indicators.note: launching here means throwing out, so a letter is ejected from the word for strike out

parts.note: to erase is to strike out or delete

indicators.note: finally takes the closing letter of enterprise

explanation.surface: Periods for going on strike, with a business finally starting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'launching' suggests starting a business, but means sending a letter away: E goes from ERASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eras are long periods of history, ages or epochs.

clue.text: Like a bear going wrong, landing in river

indicators.note: landing in puts the wrongdoing word inside the river

parts.note: the Ure is a river in Yorkshire, a crossword favourite
to sin is to go wrong morally

explanation.surface: A bear-like creature misbehaving and ending up in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursine is the adjective for bears, from Latin ursus.

clue.text: Unremarkable system for resting sixth-sevenths of the week?

definitions.text: system for resting sixth-sevenths of the week?
definitions.meaning: read as three words, a regime of labouring on one single day and resting on the other six

explanation.definitionFit: Workaday means ordinary or everyday, the opposite of special or remarkable.
